title: Eubie Blake as strict bandleader; the Pie, Pie Blackbird film
summary: Blake was busy and strict; the band toured theatres and made a short film with Nina Mae McKinney.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: He wanted me to take some drum solos, which I did. The drum solo would run around about six or seven minutes, very short, you know. I didn't have too much time.
I see. Well, how about Eubie, personality-wise, at that time? Was he a very busy man? Was he (?) with these shows?
Yeah, he was a very busy man.
Okay. And you feel that you went to him as a drummer with a background playing in the traveling shows...,
Yeah.
...so that working in a pit was not a great adjustment? Or was it... Did it present other kinds of problems for you as a drummer, merely musical problems...?
Well, when I met Eubie, I didn't have time to play no drum solos. Just play that music, back the band up. I had to change tempo about four or five different times, different numbers.
How was Eubie as a bandleader, as a director or a conductor?
He was very strict. He was strict. But... I won't say what I started to say. But I did all right, so... He was a very strict man.
Moore (II) - 27

I went... In the period after the theatre, he went to Baltimore and played a theatre, and Washington and Philadelphia, and then come on back. Then we made this picture, a short picture with Ina Mae McKinney. The name of it was Pie-Pie Blackbirds. I guess we were supposed to be the blackbirds. We was down there in this pie with these hats on, like a chef (?) pie with white hats and the white coats. We was down there. And Ina Mae McKinney, she was singing, you know... But then, that was it.
Was this one of Lew Leslie's Blackbirds acts that were...?
No. No, Lew Leslie was different.
This was slightly different.
Before that.
This was before that, yeah.
Before that.
This wasn't one of...
That was before that.
Apparently the idea was one of the residuals, though, I guess. But Eubie was strict as a bandleader...
Yes.
And he wanted his music played as he had written it out and as he had arranged...
Right.
